text:
infra-bot: ALERT 2026-03-19T03:21:12Z - token_refresh_rate anomaly for tenant "acme-corp". 10x baseline, sources: 3 distinct IPs (54.23.12.9, 18.142.33.7, 34.201.45.11). Auto-sessions revoking ~2k tokens. Investigate.

sarah: seeing this, thanks. jamal are you on call? any impact to user sessions/console? :eyes:

jamal: I'm on it. initial look — refresh endpoint (POST /auth/refresh) traffic spike. Some services report 500s, some users complaining about forced re-auth.

eli: query I ran against auth-logs:
```
select count(*) group by src_ip, status from auth_logs where event='refresh' and ts > ago(30m)
```
results: 2,180 refresh attempts from those IPs, many 429/401 errors.

maria: audit-bot linked refresh token usage stream: https://console.redwood/acme/audit/refresh-spike - large number of 'prompt_push' events, looks like MFA pushes triggered repeatedly.

sarah: do NOT rotate customer KMS keys. this looks like abusive client behavior hitting refresh loop, not key compromise. we need containment + rate limiting.

ops-oncall: putting quick mitigations in place: WAF rule added to block 54.23.12.9 and 18.142.33.7 for tenant acme-corp. command: `fwctl block --ip 54.23.12.9 --scope tenant:acme-corp`

jamal: also added temporary route to DROP refresh requests with User-Agent matching `curl/7.*` coming from those IPs. rolling out now.

eli: note: some refresh flows are performed by service accounts (svc-deploybot) — increasing suspicion of credential stuffing or leaked service token. checking RBAC for service tokens now.

maria: audit log snippet: `svc-deploybot` requested refresh 1.8k times in 20m. That service should not issue interactive refresh. potential misconfigured cron.

sarah: action items:
- [ ] confirm whether svc-deploybot private key/token rotated recently
- [ ] add server-side throttle for refresh endpoint (per-account and per-IP)
- [ ] add metric/alert for refresh:requests_per_minute per tenant
- [ ] add audit field `refresh_nonce` to correlate replayed tokens
- [ ] RBAC: prevent service accounts from using interactive refresh flow

jamal: started a short-lived tenant policy to reject refreshes > 10/min per account. will monitor for false positives.

ops-oncall: we've stopped immediate user-visible revokes, login complaints reduced. continuing monitoring.

maria: postmortem stub created: https://wiki.redwood/incident/2198765432 - tagging sec-eng and platform.

sarah: for post-incident: schedule KMS key access review, but no rotation unless evidence of compromise. add a runbook step to check refresh_nonce correlation and update docs. assign owner: @jamal.

jamal: will own follow-ups. will also push a one-week telemetry change to capture raw UA and refresh headers for correlation.

eli: final note — consider implementing signed refresh tokens with reuse-detection to prevent replay loops.

sarah: thanks all. we'll convert this thread into a brief postmortem once we have logs and RCA. closing loop here, will follow up on wiki. :white_check_mark:
